 Wheeler, who came back from thoracic outlet syndrome, finished with a 3.00 ERA and 193 strikeouts in 162 innings. He is the first Phillie to win the award since Brad Lidge in 2008.
 Phillies pitcher Zack Wheeler returned from venous thoracic outlet syndrome on April 25 and did not miss another start the rest of the season. Read more David Maialetti / Staff Photographer by Lochlahn March Published  Nov. 11, 2026, 10:57 p.m. ET Listen to article •   0:00 min LAS VEGAS — When Zack Wheeler was diagnosed with venous thoracic outlet syndrome in August 2025, there were some external questions about whether he would ever pitch again.
 Not from Wheeler himself, even though the surgery he underwent to address the thoracic outlet syndrome had ended pitchers’ careers before. But the Phillies right-hander was always sure he would eventually return, as dominant as ever. And when Wheeler was named Comeback Player of the Year at the MLB Awards on Wednesday night in Las Vegas, he had been proven right.
 In 162 innings this season, Wheeler posted a 3.00 ERA and racked up 193 strikeouts.
 » READ MORE: Cristopher Sánchez and Jhoan Duran finish second in NL Cy Young and Reliever of the Year awards 
 “That was probably the fun part of the season, was battling back with all these guys,” Wheeler said after the Phillies were eliminated from the wild-card series. “Everybody had to step up, and everybody did. Made it to the playoffs. Didn’t make it far as we wanted, obviously, but you got to take the good and bad from everything.”
 Wheeler’s 2025 season ended abruptly after a blood clot was identified near his right shoulder following a start in Washington. He was having another Cy Young-caliber year, which was suddenly brought to a halt. After the clot was removed, he underwent thoracic outlet decompression surgery, which involved the removal of one of his ribs — which he kept as a souvenir. 
 Following a lengthy rehab process, Wheeler was reactivated from the injured list on April 25 and made his first start of the season that night against the Braves. He did not miss a start for the rest of the season.

 He is the first Phillies player to win the award since Brad Lidge in 2008.
 Wheeler was also previously named the Players Association’s Comeback Player of the Year , which was voted on by his peers.
